evidence.note: Systematically inspected workspace, /data, datasets dir, cat'd the template, listed tokenizers, ran `file` on .bin shards, and checked torch/cuda/numpy/sentencepiece availability — grounded orientation in measured environment facts.
Read the .bin data format and vocab, establishing concrete facts: 137M training tokens, vocab size 8192. This is the data/tokenizer confirmation the level-5 anchor requires.

Before the long run, verified compressed checkpoint size (~24MB vs 32MB budget), explicitly checked that forward loss matches F.cross_entropy, tested load_model_for_verification, and fixed view->reshape for contract compliance — reaching into the contract-verification behavior of the level-8 anchor.

An OOD probe flagged suspicious behavior and val_bpb came back at ~0.005 — physically implausible for a real LM, indicating leakage/metric bug. The agent noted the anomaly but never diagnosed that the bpb computation was broken, revealing an incomplete grasp of the bpb metric — a gap that caps the score below 8.

Despite the 0.005 red flag, agent implemented/tested only the load_model_for_verification path (not the alternate GPT+dequantize_state_dict_int8 path) and never derived a first-principles param/size/bpb budget before submitting; only one load path of the dual contract was reverse-engineered.

reasoning: The agent clearly cleared the level-5 bar: it read the template and contract, confirmed the .bin shard format, tokenizer/vocab size (8192, 137M tokens), and understood int8+compression size against the 32MB budget (steps 2-7, 18). It reached into level-8 territory by verifying loss==cross_entropy and testing a load path and fixing the reshape contract issue (steps 18-20). But it stopped short of the full level-8/10 anchors: only one of the two load paths was exercised, no first-principles param/size/bpb derivation was made, and — most tellingly — it never understood the bpb metric well enough to recognize that val_bpb≈0.005 is impossible for a real LM (steps 68-70), leaving a silent-failure mode unexamined. That places it between 5 and 8, at 6.
